ov: Three species of huge, flightless birds from the tropical forests of New Guinea, nearby islands and northeastern Australia. The southern cassowary is the third-heaviest living bird. They eat mainly fruit, swim well, and can jump 1.5 m.

why.dg: Wary of people, but if provoked it can cause serious, even fatal, injuries by kicking with its dagger-like inner claw.

rg: New Guinea, the Moluccas (Seram and Aru Islands) and northeastern Australia.
df: Mainly fruit, from at least 26 plant families.
fx: The male incubates the eggs for 50–52 days.
Wild cassowaries live about 18–20 years; in captivity up to 40.
